clue.text: Steps taken to provide charitable support?

definitions.text: Steps taken to provide charitable support?

parts.words: Steps taken to provide charitable support
parts.note: the steps are literal footsteps, taken by walkers who have collected pledges for a charity

explanation.surface: Someone asks what measures were put in place to help a good cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps taken' reads as 'measures adopted', but here the steps are actual paces walked for money pledged to charity.
explanation.definitionFit: A fundraising event where participants collect pledges per mile covered on foot.

clue.text: Actor Olivier, say, adopting right style

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the peer takes the other pieces into himself

parts.note: Laurence Olivier was made a life peer, so he is an example of a peer
form means style or manner

explanation.surface: Laurence Olivier the actor takes on a correct manner on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Olivier sat in the House of Lords as Baron Olivier; 'adopting' means the peer takes the right-plus-style pieces into his middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone who acts on stage or screen is a type of entertainer appearing before an audience.

clue.text: Idiot seen in bar in New York

indicators.note: the bar is placed in the abbreviation for New York, inside its two letters

parts.note: an inn is a pub or bar

explanation.surface: A fool is spotted drinking in a Manhattan bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a silly, foolish person or simpleton.

clue.text: Zero (representation of absence) almost entirely egg-shaped

parts.note: zero looks like the letter O
a void is an empty space, a picture of nothing being there

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: entirely means all, wholly

explanation.surface: A geometric description of something nearly perfectly oval, with a nod to nothingness.
explanation.definitionFit: From the Latin for egg: having an oval outline like a hen's egg.

clue.text: Letter giving English no sign of speech impediment, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things backwards, so these words are read in reverse

parts.note: a lisp is a typical speech impediment

explanation.surface: A letter written in plain English shows no trace of a stammer when looked back on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' reads 'no lisp' backwards, giving PSILON, which follows the E.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Blemish covering a couple of lines on church display area

indicators.note: the blemish wraps around the other pieces, covering them

parts.note: a wart is a blemish on the skin
L is the abbreviation for line, so two lines give LL

explanation.surface: A mark spoils a couple of lines on a church noticeboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' wraps the blemish round the inner pieces, which go in after its first letter; 'on' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A large poster or chart pinned up on a wall to show information to a room.

clue.text: Schooling obviously includes this language

indicators.note: the phrase includes the answer within its letters, across the word break

explanation.surface: Education naturally involves learning a tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' points to the answer sitting inside 'schooLING Obviously'.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal word for a language, often foreign or specialist jargon.

clue.text: One who expounds on certain points?

definitions.text: One who expounds on certain points?

parts.words: One who expounds on certain points
parts.note: the points are the tips of foils and épées, and the expert teaches the art of using them

explanation.surface: A lecturer who holds forth on particular matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'certain points' looks like topics of debate, but the points are weapon tips in swordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher of swordsmanship, who instructs pupils in using a foil, épée or sabre.

clue.text: Newspapers getting the meat on what politicians do on visits?

parts.note: the press means newspapers collectively
flesh is meat

explanation.surface: Reporters cover the food at a politician's walkabout.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for shaking hands and mingling with the public, as campaigning politicians do.

clue.text: Certain to retract about one or other being mistaken

indicators.note: about means around, so the reversed word goes around the rearranged letters
to retract means to draw back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: sure means certain

indicators.note: other means different, so the letters of the preceding words are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone sure of themselves backs down because one party or the other got it wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retract' gives ERUS; 'other' gives RONEO, an arrangement of 'one or' different from the printed one; 'about' puts the second inside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: wrong, incorrect or based on a mistake.

clue.text: Individual beset by both sides — but following neither?

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the individual is enclosed by the sides

parts.note: L and R stand for left and right, the two sides
one means an individual person

explanation.surface: A person caught between two factions who joins neither camp.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'sides': someone who follows neither side keeps to themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitary person keeps apart and takes no part in any group or faction.

clue.text: Uproar about working associate

indicators.note: about means around, so the uproar goes around the other piece

parts.note: a cry is a loud outcry or uproar
on means working or functioning, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A colleague causes a fuss at the office.
explanation.definitionFit: A close companion or pal, often with a hint of favouritism.

clue.text: Very enjoyable composer enthralling one in company

indicators.note: enthralling means captivating, read as holding something inside

parts.note: Frederick Delius was an English composer

indicators.note: the one is placed in the abbreviation for company

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A composer charming one of the company provides a delightful performance.
explanation.walkthrough: I in CO gives CIO, which DELIUS holds: DELI-CIO-US.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in the sense of highly pleasing or delightful, not only of food.

clue.text: Minor interaction of man and lion

indicators.note: interaction suggests the two words mixing together, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small encounter between a man and a big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: token or very small, as a nominal fee.

clue.text: Jazzy thing supported by one in suit?

definitions.text: Jazzy thing supported by one in suit?

parts.words: Jazzy thing supported by one in suit
parts.note: a lively music venue backed by a card from one of the four suits, the second half of the name being a card suit

explanation.surface: Something flashy is backed by a businessman in a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'suit' reads as clothing, but a club is one of the four suits in a pack of cards; the venue plays jazz late in the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: A late-opening entertainment venue with music, drinks and dancing.

clue.text: Close members of family are within home

indicators.note: within means inside, so the word is placed inside the home

parts.note: a nest is a home, especially a bird's

explanation.surface: Relatives who live nearby are in the family home.
explanation.definitionFit: As a plural noun, 'one's nearest' are one's immediate relations, as in 'nearest and dearest'.

clue.text: Crime is up, badly? It comes of hankering after the finer things of life

definitions.text: hankering after the finer things of life

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of the preceding words are put together wrongly, rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that rising crime stems from people wanting luxuries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' looks like the verb 'is up' meaning rising, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Devotion to refined pleasures, especially good food and drink, named after the philosopher Epicurus.

clue.text: Perfect partner's strength, holding king and queen

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the strength encloses the royal pieces

parts.note: might means strength or power
R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king
R is the abbreviation for regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: An ideal spouse's power holds sway over a king and queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for the ideal husband or boyfriend someone hopes to find.

clue.text: Reprimand, as mark of success not available

parts.note: a tick marks a correct answer
off means not available, as a dish off the menu

explanation.surface: A telling-off when a sign of achievement is withheld.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British phrase meaning to scold or tell someone off.

clue.text: Isotherm potentially carrier of important information?

definitions.meaning: an isotherm is a line on a map joining places of equal temperature, so it could be a line marking heat
a direct telephone link kept for urgent messages

explanation.definitionFit: A weather-map line of high temperature, and a dedicated phone link for urgent calls, such as between heads of state.

clue.text: Weapon carrier long carried by army supported by monarch

indicators.note: in a down clue, supported by means the monarch comes underneath, after the other piece
carried by means held inside, so the letter for long sits within the army

parts.note: a host is an army or great multitude
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A gun case is carried by soldiers serving the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A leather case worn on the belt or shoulder for a pistol.

clue.text: Dubious castle pic, retouched

indicators.note: retouched means altered, as a photo is, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Doubts arise about a doctored photograph of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: doubtful or unconvinced.

clue.text: Source of inspiration in period fashion, mostly

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: ton is an old word for fashion or the fashionable set

explanation.surface: Inspiration found in the style of a bygone age, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: ERATO is the Greek Muse of lyric and love poetry; the Muses are crosswords' usual 'sources of inspiration'.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the nine Muses, the goddesses who inspired poets and artists.

clue.text: Regret doing for girl's insides with poor-quality food

indicators.note: doing for means replacing, so the regret takes the place of the inner letters

parts.note: the word girl taken as written
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Remorse over a girl's stomach after a nasty meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'insides' are the inner letters IR of GIRL; RUE replaces them, G-RUE-L.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin, watery porridge, the stereotype of meagre institutional fare.

clue.text: Sabotaged energy? Rubbish

parts.note: go means energy or drive
tat is cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone's drive was undermined, and it's nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb meaning tampered with, bribed or interfered with.

clue.text: I will block returning implausible communication

indicators.note: to block is to stop up a gap, so the letter sits in the middle of the other word
returning means going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: lame means unconvincing or implausible, as a lame excuse

explanation.surface: Someone vows to stop a weak excuse coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns LAME into EMAL, and I goes in it: EMA-I-L.
explanation.definitionFit: An electronic message sent over the internet.

clue.text: Does better than free sex-shows?

parts.note: out means free, as a released prisoner is out
strips are striptease shows

explanation.surface: A question whether risqué shows cost nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: surpasses or exceeds.

clue.text: When can police arrest illegal drinkers — we've been waiting!

definitions.text: When can police arrest illegal drinkers — we've been waiting!

parts.words: When can police arrest illegal drinkers — we've been waiting
parts.note: drinking after closing time is illegal, so the police must wait until the pub's closing hour has passed; the second part is the idiom of impatience

explanation.surface: Impatient onlookers wonder when officers will finally act against after-hours drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: British pubs had a legal closing time; drinking after it was an offence, so police could only act once that time had passed.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom said when something happens later than it should have, at long last.
